newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares end the week down, outlook volatile.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares end the week down, outlook volatile.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Friday hit by profit-taking in key blue chip Novo Nordisk and foreign market declines in the wake of overnight U.S. falls with dealers unable to foresee next week's trend.

"The market rallied a little from earlier falls but profit-taking in Novo quashed the recovery. The market is still basically positive but given the present volatility of Wall Street, it is difficult to predict anything," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.29 point or 0.99 percent down at 129.35, after falling to 128.92 at its lowest, while the KFX December future fell 1.75 point to 129.25.
1,603 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns were traded in the KFX December future.
Novo Nordisk plunged 40 crowns to 1,050, while FLS shed 20 crowns to finish at 740. ISS was the day's most traded paper with 278,000 shares changing hands to close three crowns lower at 159.
B&O continued to benefit from its upward adjustment of its expected first-half 1996/97 result, putting on 12 crowns to end at 280.
The day's turnover was 1.074 billion crowns.
